why_this_cell: The THIRD production-ready cell and the first outside TypeScript. Its purpose is to prove the newly wired Python validator, so the operation is held constant with the TypeScript cell -- a failure here is then attributable to validation rather than to an unexercised codemod.

consumer.install_note: The venv MUST live inside the mounted volume. pip installs into the container's own site-packages by default, which the read-only check container does not have -- the first draft did that and mypy was simply not found in phase two. The venv is the Python equivalent of node_modules.

expect.fix_target_note: The DECLARATION is stale, not the usages -- same inversion as the TypeScript change-field-type cell. The file that ERRORS (src/contact.py) must be repaired without being edited.

transformation.action: rewrite the phone_number annotation from int to str
transformation.why: the contract now says string; the annotation is simply wrong and there is exactly one correct value for it

hazards.hazard: mypy's reach depends on the CONSUMER's annotations, unlike tsc which reads the project config
hazards.measured: The same broken file passes mypy at exit 0 once the parameter annotation is removed. compileall -- the toolchain the registry originally DECLARED for python -- passes the broken consumer at exit 0 too, which is why it was replaced rather than wired.
hazards.mitigation: The runner passes --disallow-untyped-defs and splits the result three ways by error code: any non-no-untyped-def error is INVALID, only-no-untyped-def is UNABLE_TO_VALIDATE, no errors is VALID. A partially annotated consumer therefore cannot reach AUTO. Guarded by test_python_validator_refuses_to_pass_an_unannotated_consumer.
hazards.fixture_requirement: Every def in this fixture is annotated. That is load-bearing, not stylistic.

hazards.hazard: _change_type_python is field-blind -- it rewrites every occurrence of the old annotation and never reads field_name
hazards.fixture_requirement: src/models.py declares exactly one int-annotated field. A second would be silently retyped and the minimal-diff assertion would fail. This is a real codemod limitation, not a fixture one.

hazards.hazard: The codemod does not respect comments or docstrings
hazards.measured: The first draft of this fixture wrote the annotation pattern out literally in its module docstring and the codemod reported "3 type annotation(s) updated" for a one-field change -- two of them inside the comment. The TypeScript sibling fixture had the identical flaw and was corrected at the same time; there the rewritten comment became self-contradictory, claiming exactly one string-annotated property when there were then four.
hazards.mitigation: Both fixtures' prose now describes the annotation instead of quoting it. The test asserts exactly ONE line differs, so a comment rewrite fails the cell rather than inflating it.

not_this_cell.why_not: The Python remove_field codemod DOES NOT WORK. Measured before this fixture was written: given a consumer reading user.phone_number in an f-string and a dict literal, apply_fix_template returns the file with EVERY reference still present, while reporting "Removed references to field 'phone_number' (2 lines affected)" -- a false claim in a user-facing string. It also collapses blank lines, so it produces a spurious diff while achieving nothing. Same defect shape as the Stage 4 TypeScript baseline that forced app/ts_codemod.py to be written. python/openapi/remove_field is therefore NOT production-ready and a fixture for it would correctly fail at the typecheck step.
not_this_cell.also_broken: python type_removed leaves the type name in place while claiming removal. python field_renamed and field_type_changed both genuinely transform.

measured.ripple_explanation: Changed type 'int' -> 'str' in python code (contract: integer -> string). 1 type annotation(s) updated.
ripple_edits: dataclass field annotation: phone_number int -> str
measured.untouched_verified_by: byte comparison of src/contact.py, src/orders.py, src/__init__.py, mypy.ini, requirements-dev.txt
measured.validation_backend: docker, python:3.11-alpine, --network none and read-only source for the typecheck
measured.cost_note: This cell needed a VALIDATOR, unlike the second cell which needed only a fixture. Wiring python took validate_ok from 63 cells to 126 and left 33 python mechanical cells blocked on nothing but a fixture -- though for remove_field and type_removed the codemod is the real blocker, and a fixture would expose that rather than close it.
